what_the_model_does: A small free-standing gearbox: one input shaft (bottom) drives one output shaft (top-right) through a pair of gears on a common main shaft. A ball-stud lever slides a dog-clutch collar along the main shaft, which is meant to pick between two gear paths for two different output speeds (or possibly just engage/disengage drive -- see open_questions).
open_questions: What exactly the dog-clutch sleeve (sleeve-wht-Q, sleeve-blk-S) selects between is not confirmed. gear-gray-L is catalogued as a locked (cross-hole) gear, always turning with the main shaft, which doesn't fit a classic 2-speed design where the clutch should pick between two FREE gears. gear-red-P is the only confirmed free gear. The booklet pictures aren't clear enough to settle whether gear-gray-L is really free (and the catalog match is wrong) or whether this model's '2-speed' is actually an engage/disengage clutch rather than two different ratios.

Whether gear-blue-U (the input gear) meshes only with gear-gray-L, or also reaches gear-red-P's teeth (both are 16-tooth, close together), is not shown clearly. If it meshes with both, the clutch is choosing which of two always-spinning gears gets locked to the output shaft (an engage/disengage clutch). If only gear-gray-L, then gear-red-P needs a second, unseen drive path to make sense as a '2nd speed' -- not found in this booklet.

fork-J's exact part number could not be confirmed from the catalog (see step 6's review_note) -- its shape (slot straddling the clutch sleeve, ball stud on top for a lever) is read from position and function, not a confirmed match.
The left-side bush-K and right-side fork-R bearing holes for the main shaft are read from the picture's rough layout, not confirmed hole-by-hole (see steps 7 and 11's review_notes).

systems.name: Frame / housing
systems.real_machine: The casing of a real gearbox: a rigid box that holds the shafts at fixed spacing so the gears stay meshed.
systems.purpose: A U-shaped frame (a 7-hole beam on two corner posts) that all the shafts and the shift mechanism mount to.
systems.why_built_first: Every shaft, gear and the shift fork need something rigid to hang off; the frame has to close into a U before anything can be mounted at a fixed spacing.

parts.bracket-L: Left corner post: anchors pin-blue-A (holds the beam) and pin-red-A (unused stub in this 11-step booklet).
parts.pin-red-A: Free stub on the left corner; not reached again in this booklet.
parts.bracket-R: Right corner post: anchors peg-black-B (holds the beam).
parts.fork-R: Right-hand bearing block: its round hole is where the main shaft axle-N spins free and exits the frame.
parts.beam-C: Top bar: closes the frame into a U and carries the shift mechanism's mounting pegs.
parts.pin-blue-D: Carries bracket-G, the input shaft's bearing post.
parts.pin-blue-F: Carries bracket-H, a second bearing post next to the output side.
parts.bracket-G: Bearing post for axle-input-T, the input shaft.
parts.bracket-H: Bearing post next to gear-tan-M / the output end.
parts.pin-blue-E: Carries fork-J, the shift-fork housing, in the middle of the frame.

systems.name: Gear-shift lever and fork
systems.real_machine: The gear stick and selector fork of a manual gearbox: moving the lever slides a collar inside the box to pick a gear.
systems.purpose: Lets a person (through a lever, not included, plugged onto knob-I's ball) slide the dog-clutch sleeve along the main shaft.
systems.why_built_first: Built before the main shaft (steps 7-10) so the shaft can be threaded through its slot as the shaft goes in.

parts.fork-J: Housing with a slot that straddles the sliding clutch sleeve; a ball stud on top takes a lever.
parts.knob-I: Ball-stud lever attachment point on top of fork-J.

systems.name: Gear shaft and clutch
systems.real_machine: The gear cluster of a 2-speed transmission: an input shaft, an output shaft, two gears, and a clutch that picks between them.
systems.purpose: Carries drive from the input handle (axle-input-T) to the output handle (via axle-N), through whichever gear the dog-clutch currently selects.
systems.why_built_first: Built last since every gear and the clutch sleeve mount on the main shaft, which needs the frame and the shift fork's slot already in place to thread through.

parts.bush-K: Spacer/stop near the main shaft's left end, locked to axle-N.
parts.gear-gray-L: Gear locked to axle-N; meshes with the input gear gear-blue-U.
parts.gear-tan-M: Gear locked to axle-N near the output end; always turns with the main shaft.
parts.axle-N: The main shaft: carries bush-K, gear-gray-L, the clutch sleeve, gear-red-P (free) and gear-tan-M, and exits through fork-R and ext-W as the output.
parts.axle-brown-O: Short axle gear-red-P free-spins on, positioned in line with the main shaft.
parts.gear-red-P: Free clutch gear between gear-gray-L and gear-tan-M; the dog-clutch sleeve can lock it to the shaft.
parts.sleeve-wht-Q: Half of the sliding dog-clutch collar, locked to axle-N, slides in fork-J's slot.
parts.sleeve-blk-S: Other half of the sliding dog-clutch collar, locked to axle-N next to sleeve-wht-Q.
parts.axle-input-T: Input shaft, turned by hand or motor at ext-V; meshes gear-blue-U into gear-gray-L.
parts.gear-blue-U: Input gear on axle-input-T; drives gear-gray-L.
parts.ext-V: Input handle, the exposed end of axle-input-T.
parts.ext-W: Output handle, the exposed end of axle-N.
